short: The unique hash the invoice portal returns when an e-invoice is registered.
seoTitle: What Is Invoice Reference Number? Meaning and Example
metaDescription: The invoice reference number, or IRN, is a 64-character hash generated when an invoice is successfully registered on the invoice registration portal.
definition: The invoice reference number, or IRN, is a 64-character hash generated when an invoice is successfully registered on the invoice registration portal. It is unique to the supplier GSTIN, document type, number and financial year, so the same invoice can never be registered twice.
bodyHtml:
Why Invoice Reference Number matters

The IRN and the signed QR code are what prove an e-invoice is genuine. Customers and auditors read them to confirm the document was actually reported rather than printed locally.

How Invoice Reference Number works in practice

Print the IRN and the signed QR code on the invoice you hand over. Because the hash includes the invoice number and financial year, restarting your invoice numbering each year has to be done carefully to avoid clashes.

faq.question: Can two invoices share an IRN?
faq.answer: No. The hash is built from the supplier GSTIN, document type, number and financial year, so duplicates are rejected.

faq.question: Is the IRN the same as the invoice number?
faq.answer: No. The invoice number is yours; the IRN is generated by the portal when the invoice is registered.
